items.readable_text:
Content:
A perfect square trinomial is a three-term expression that is the result of squaring a binomial.

Content:
For example, the expression
[MATH: x^2 + 6x + 9]
is a perfect square trinomial because it is the result of squaring the binomial [MATH: (x+3)], as shown below:

Content:
[MATH: (x + 3)^{2}|=; x^{2} + 2 ⋅ 3x + 3^{2}|=; x^{2} + 6x + 9]

Content:
To factor a perfect square trinomial, we have to figure out what binomial it is the square of. We can often do this by relating the perfect square trinomial to the square of a sum:
[MATH: x^2 + {\color{red}2} {\color{blue}a}x + {\color{blue}a}^2 = (x + {\color{blue}a})^2]

Content:
To illustrate, let's factor the expression [MATH: x^2+6x+9] using the square of sum formula. We perform the following steps:

Content:
1. Write the constant term as a perfect square:
[MATH: x^{2} + 6x + 3^{2}]
2. Factor a [MATH: 2] out of the linear term:
[MATH: x^{2} + 2 ⋅ 3x + 3^{2}]
3. Factor the trinomial using the "square of a sum formula". In this case, we have [MATH: {\color{blue}{a}}={\color{blue}{3}}\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: (x + 3)^{2}]

Content:
This method works only when the trinomial is a perfect square! It will not work for every trinomial. We will learn more general methods in the future.

items.title: Factoring a Trinomial Generated by the Square of a Sum

sections.normalized_html:
The "square of a sum" formula states that

[MATH: x^2 + {\color{red}{2}}{\color{blue}{a}} x + a^2 = (x+{\color{blue}{a}})^2 .]

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

[MATH: x^2 + 12x + 36.]

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

[MATH: x^{2} + 12x + 6^{2}]

Then, we factor a [MATH: 2] out of the linear term:

[MATH: x^{2} + 2 ⋅ 6x + 6^{2}]

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of sum formula with [MATH: {\color{blue}{a}} = {\color{blue}{6}}.] This gives

[MATH: (x + 6)^{2}.]
